tips: When you stop, the last letter drops its haraka and takes a sukoon:  رَ ← رۡ   We still write the word as it is in the Mushaf.
Stop on ـٌ or ـٍ: the tanween drops and the letter takes a sukoon:  دٌ ← دۡ
Stop on ـً: say an alif instead, 2 counts (madd iwad):  مًا ← مَا
Taa marbuta ة: keep reading → say ت  ·  stop → say هۡ
Even with ةً you stop with هۡ — no alif. Right box: keep going. Left box: stop.
Stop right after a madd letter: stretch it 2, 4 or 6 counts (madd aarid). Pick one and keep it the same.
A qalqala letter at the stop still bounces:  بۡ  دۡ
ل has no sukoon, next letter has a shadda: skip the ل.  Starting here: say ٱ as أَ.
Starting with this word: say ٱ as أَ.
Stopping on it: the last letter takes a sukoon.
Sukoon on the ل and no shadda after it: say the ل clearly.
Starting with this word: say ٱ as أَ.
Stopping on it: the last letter takes a sukoon.
Qat' أ إ is always said. Wasl ٱ (small ص on top) is said أَ only when you start with it.
Joined to what comes before: ٱ is silent. Read straight into the next letter.
Sun letter: ٱ and ل are both silent:  وَٱلتِّينِ ← وَتِّ
Two sakin letters meet: one must move. The tanween's noon takes a kasra:  خَيۡرًا ٱلۡ ← خَيۡرَنِ لۡ
Hams = whisper. With كۡ let a little air flow out, like a soft whisper.
Middle or end of the word, the air still flows. At the end, stop softly — no bounce.

items.caption: [تۡ middle]   ·   ي + تۡ + ل + و + ن

tips: Hams = whisper. With تۡ let a little air flow out, like a soft whisper.
Say تۡ softly with a little air — it is not a qalqala letter, so no bounce.
Heavy letters خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ: full, deep sound. With a kasra, خ غ ق get a little lighter.
Kasra makes only خ غ ق less heavy. Fatha or damma keeps them fully heavy.
These never get lighter: ص ض ط ظ. Even صِ ضِ طِ ظِ stay fully heavy.
Same deep sound in all three boxes.
The ل of ٱللَّه is heavy after fatha or damma (or when you start), light after kasra. Every other ل is light.
لِلَّهِ is a short spelling: لِ + ٱللَّه. The ٱ and one ل are not written.

tips: فِرۡقٍ: heavy or light when you keep reading; heavy when you stop on it.
مِصۡرَ and ٱلۡقِطۡرِ: heavy or light only when you stop. Preferred: مِصۡرَ heavy, ٱلۡقِطۡرِ light.

items.caption: [ا Silent]   ·   لُواْ
items.rule: Round zero: قَالُواْ: the alif with a round zero is never said

items.caption: [ا Silent]   ·   نُواْ
items.rule: Round zero: قَالُواْ: the alif with a round zero is never said

items.caption: [ا Silent]   ·   رُواْ
items.rule: Round zero: قَالُواْ: the alif with a round zero is never said

items.caption: [ا Say at stop]   ·   نَا۠
items.rule: Rectangular zero: أَنَا۠: silent when you keep reading; when you stop, say a short alif (2 counts)

items.caption: [ا Say at stop]   ·   نَّا۠
items.rule: Rectangular zero: أَنَا۠: silent when you keep reading; when you stop, say a short alif (2 counts)

items.caption: [ا Say at stop]   ·   رَا۠
items.rule: Rectangular zero: أَنَا۠: silent when you keep reading; when you stop, say a short alif (2 counts)

tips: Small zero on an alif: round = never said. Rectangle = said only when you stop.
Waqf signs sit above the last word. They tell you where to stop or keep reading.
